summary: Inject prompt-level skepticism for tool failures/negatives to counter uncritical acceptance of VQA 'No' outputs.

edits.hypothesis: Adding explicit instructions to treat tool failures and 'not_applicable' statuses as missing evidence, and to be skeptical of general VQA negative findings, will prevent the agent from incorrectly concluding 'no' when pathology is present but missed by tools.
edits.why_not_lower_lever: The failure mode is behavioral (how the agent weighs conflicting/missing evidence), which is best addressed by adjusting the decision policy in the system prompt rather than changing control flow or tool wrappers.
edits.trigger_condition: always (applies to all M5 tasks via the ANSWER constant used in agent_system)
edits.retroactive_check: (corrective) In q000001, the agent would have treated the roi_crop KeyError as missing evidence and relied more on its own visual inspection of the trachea, potentially identifying the disease. In q000002, the agent would have been skeptical of the two 'No' responses from CheXagent and LLaVA-Med, especially given the maira2 'not_applicable' status, and performed a more careful visual check. (preservative) The change adds skepticism but does not force tool use or break the habit of skipping tools for simple tasks (q000003). (transfer) Generalizes to any task where tools fail or return false negatives.
edits.regression_risk: May increase false positives if the agent becomes overly skeptical of correct negative findings, but the instruction emphasizes 'visual inspection' which should ground the decision.
edits.mechanism: Adding explicit instructions to treat tool failures and 'not_applicable' statuses as missing evidence, and to be skeptical of general VQA negative findings, will prevent the agent from incorrectly concluding 'no' when pathology is present but missed by tools.
